reviewed_not_included.reason: Could not be matched to an authoritative shutdown event on any standard channel. Not treated as a shutdown event.
Process termination is routine and has no anomaly meaning on its own.
Logoff; routine.
User-initiated logoff; routine.
Privileged service called; extremely high volume (Audit Sensitive Privilege Use).
Operation on privileged object; extremely high volume.
Per-user audit policy table created; logged at every boot.
Security event source registration; routine at service start.
Service control request sent; routine (legacy event).
Service entered running/stopped state; very high routine volume.
WFP permitted bind to a local port; very high volume, no anomaly meaning.
Sysmon process creation; telemetry volume. Note that ID 1 in the System log is a different event (several providers use it), which is why rules are keyed on channel + ID.
Sysmon network connection; telemetry volume.
Sysmon process terminated; telemetry.
ID 1 in the System log is shared by several providers (Kernel-General, Power-Troubleshooter and others); an ID-only rule would mislabel events. 4616 covers time changes.
Only generated by a specific monitored-pattern configuration; add if your environment uses it.
Only relevant where CrashOnAuditFail is configured; 4906 covers changes to that setting.
DPAPI master-key backup is routine in domains (automatic backup to a DC).
Computer account created; routine domain join noise.
Firewall policy read/parse errors (5027-5029) are operational faults; 5025/5030/5034 cover protection being down.
Group Policy firewall refresh; routine.
ASR audit-mode event; organisations running ASR in audit mode generate large volumes. 1121 (block) is included.
Temporary WMI event registrations are created constantly by management software.
Code integrity page-hash failures are frequent for some legitimate drivers; 5038 is included.
Driver loaded; noisy unless the Sysmon config filters it.
ProcessAccess; volume depends entirely on Sysmon config.
FileExecutableDetected; noisy on build/dev hosts.
